# `silk/system/host_input_native`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The native provider of the `HostInput` effect: command-line arguments, environment, and the
working directory.

## When to use
A native `main` that requires `&mut HostInput` gets this provider from `silk.platform.native.start`. To
make one yourself, capture a `NativeHostInput` from `silk.platform.native.host_input`, and pass it to
[`OsHostInput.make`](#OsHostInput.impl.make).

## Details
The arguments and the environment come from the snapshot, so they do not change. The working
directory is read from the process at each call. Each result is a new owned copy.

## Gotchas
The provider exists only on Darwin on aarch64, and Linux with GNU libc on x86_64 or aarch64.

## Examples
### Read the working directory
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.collections.bytes { Bytes }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.system.host_input { HostInput, HostInputError }
import silk.platform.native.host_input { NativeHostInput }
import silk.system.host_input_native { OsHostInput }

effect fn program() -> i32
  ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator {
  // A snapshot of the environment, with no arguments. No other code changes the environment now.
  let snapshot = run unsafe NativeHostInput.environmentSnapshot()
  let mut inputs = OsHostInput.make(move snapshot)
  let count = run HostInput.argumentCount() |> Effect.provideMut<HostInput>(&mut inputs)
  let directory = run HostInput.workingDirectory() |> Effect.provideMut<HostInput>(&mut inputs)

  // The working directory is an absolute path.
  let path = Bytes.asSlice(&directory)
  if count != 0 || path.length == 0 || path[0] != 47 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn failed<E>(error: E) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 1
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(program(), failed) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

Import as `OsHostInput` with `import silk.system.host_input_native { OsHostInput }`.

## `OsHostInput`

```silk
pub struct OsHostInput
```

The native `HostInput` provider. It owns a snapshot of the arguments and the environment.

A native `main` that requires `&mut HostInput` gets one from `silk.platform.native.start`. The
arguments and the environment come from the snapshot, so they do not change. The working
directory is read from the process at each call. Each result is a new owned copy.
